items.followUp: Write the HTML tag used to underline text.

rubric.why: Identifies a valid bold-text tag and shows how it encloses text.
rubric.description: Gives a valid opening and closing bold tag.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correct paired tag; 1 mark if only the correct tag name is given.

modelAnswer: Use the <B> tag to make text bold.
Example: Bold text

items.followUp: What is an ordered list in HTML? Write its tag.

rubric.why: States what information a definition list contains.
rubric.description: Defines a definition list as a list of terms and their definitions or descriptions.

rubric.why: Names the tags used to create a definition list and its entries.

modelAnswer: A definition list displays terms along with their definitions or descriptions.
It uses the <DL> tag; <DT> marks a term and <DD> gives its definition or description.

items.followUp: Explain what an IP address identifies and describe the parts of an IPv4 address.

rubric.why: An IP address is used to identify a device on a network.
rubric.description: Explains that an IP address identifies a device on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the identification purpose.

rubric.why: IPv4 addresses have a fixed length of 32 bits.
rubric.description: States the length of an IPv4 address.

rubric.why: The address indicates the network to which the device belongs.
rubric.description: Identifies the network part of an IP address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the network part.

rubric.why: The address distinguishes the device within its network.
rubric.description: Identifies the host part of an IP address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the host part.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a unique logical address used to identify a device on a network.
An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and is commonly written as four numbers separated by dots.
It has a network part that identifies the network.
It has a host part that identifies a device on that network.

items.followUp: Name two methods that can be used to represent an algorithm.

rubric.why: An algorithm is a strategy for planning the steps of a solution.
rubric.description: Names algorithm as one solution-planning strategy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid strategy.

rubric.why: Flowcharts, pseudocode and decision tables are also valid planning strategies.
rubric.description: Names a second valid solution-planning strategy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any other valid strategy.

modelAnswer: Two strategies for planning a solution are:
1. Algorithm
2. Flowchart

items.followUp: What information should be recorded in a trace table?

rubric.why: A trace table follows how variable values change as the algorithm runs.
rubric.description: States that a trace table records variable values during execution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning values of variables or steps.

rubric.why: Tracing helps check an algorithm's logic and can reveal errors.
rubric.description: Explains a purpose of using a trace table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid purpose.

modelAnswer: A trace table records the values of variables as an algorithm is executed, step by step.
It is used to check the logic of the algorithm and to find errors.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a container tag and an empty tag?

rubric.why: HTML tags are commonly classified into two types.
rubric.description: States the number of types of HTML tags.

rubric.why: One type has opening and closing tags; the other has no closing tag.
rubric.description: Names the two types of tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both container/paired and empty/unpaired tags.

modelAnswer: There are two types of tags in HTML:
1. Container (paired) tags
2. Empty (unpaired) tags

items.followUp: Write the base and digits used in the hexadecimal number system.

rubric.why: Hexadecimal is a base-16 number system.
Hexadecimal uses the ten decimal digits and six letters for values ten through fifteen.
rubric.description: Gives the symbols used in hexadecimal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying 0–9 and A–F.

modelAnswer: The hexadecimal system is a number system with base 16.
It uses the digits 0 to 9 and the letters A to F.
